History & Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
53-year-old man with 1-week history of painless, slightly warm swelling over the left olecranon; video exam consistent with olecranon bursitis. NSAID therapy started and blood-work arranged to exclude infectious, crystal, and inflammatory causes.

History:
• Presenting complaint: New “weird swelling” over left elbow noticed while showering ~1 week ago.  
• Course: Unchanged over the week; no progressive increase in size or pain reported.  
• Character: Soft, fluctuant (“can feel a bit of fluid”), mildly warm, minimal tenderness just lateral to tip; no marked redness.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, malaise, joint stiffness elsewhere, limitation of elbow movement. Full range of motion preserved.  
• Exacerbating / relieving factors: None identified; no prior episodes.  
• Trauma / activity: Denies any blow to elbow; works at desk, not a manual job. Runs 2–3×/week.  
• Review of systems (pertinent): No skin rash/eczema, no other joint swelling, no recent infections.  

Past Medical History:
• Osteoarthritis – GP-diagnosed “a few years ago”; joints occasionally painful (details limited).  
• Allergy – Peanut allergy (reaction details not provided).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.  
• No known drug allergies.

Medications:
• None on a regular basis.  
• Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily “after food” started today (OTC; dose/route/frequency documented).

Social History:
• Occupation: Desk job.  
• Exercise: Runs 2–3 times per week.  
• Smoking: Not discussed.  
• Alcohol / Recreational drugs: Not discussed.

Family History:
• No known family history of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other rheumatologic disease.

Physical Examination: (video)
• General: Appears well, comfortable.  
• Left elbow: Visible localized swelling over olecranon; overlying skin dry; slightly warmer than adjacent skin; minimal focal tenderness adjacent to tip; no obvious erythema; full active range of motion.  
• No other joint abnormalities visualized.  
• Vitals: Not recorded.

Investigations:
• Planned: Blood panel to include CBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatologic antibodies, serum urate, and infection screen. Forms to be mailed; results expected in ~6 days.  
• No imaging ordered at this stage.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Left olecranon swelling, likely aseptic bursitis  
  • Assessment: Clinical presentation favors non-infectious bursitis; mild warmth warrants exclusion of septic bursitis, gout, and rheumatologic causes.  
  • Plan:  
    – Start NSAID: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food; stop if gastrointestinal adverse effects.  
    – Blood tests as above to evaluate inflammatory markers, infection, urate, autoantibodies.  
    – Education: Condition not life-threatening; avoid leaning on elbow; monitor for worsening redness, pain, spreading warmth, or systemic symptoms.  
    – Safety-net: If severe pain, increasing redness, or systemic illness develops, contact service urgently for possible face-to-face assessment to rule out septic arthritis/bursitis.  
    – Follow-up: Arrange video or in-person review after blood results (~1 week).  

Issue 2 – Osteoarthritis (background)  
  • Stable; no current management requested.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis – High likelihood; classic painless swelling, slight warmth, preserved function, no systemic features.  
2. Septic olecranon bursitis – Moderate likelihood; warmth and tenderness require exclusion despite lack of systemic signs.  
3. Gouty olecranon bursitis – Low-moderate likelihood; patient demographic fits, being screened with serum urate (no prior gout history).

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Vitals, full medication list verification, smoking/alcohol history, detailed allergy reaction description.  
● Conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor incomplete sentences but clinically adequate.
